findings.text: Code calls .Elem() on parameter type without checking if it's a pointer/kind that supports Elem(). If a functional option takes a non-pointer parameter (e.g., func(Server) instead of func(*Server)), this will panic at runtime.
Code calls actualOpts.Len() without verifying actual is a slice/array/map. If actual is not a slice type, this will panic. No type guard before the Len() call on line 110.

When reporting mismatched values, both expectedFmt and actualFmt use expectedNames[i] instead of using actualNames[i] for actualFmt. This produces incorrect error output showing the wrong function name for the actual value.

Condition 'name != reflect.TypeOf(actual).String() && tValue.Len() != 0' short-circuits when expected is empty, skipping type mismatch detection. An empty FunctionalOptionsArgument would incorrectly match any actual type.

0.reason: The code calls .Elem() on the parameter type without checking if it is a pointer, which will panic for non-pointer functional option parameters.

1.reason: The code calls actualOpts.Len() without verifying actual is a slice/array/map, which will panic if actual is not a slice type.

2.reason: In the mismatch reporting, actualFmt uses expectedNames[i] instead of actualNames[i], producing incorrect error output.

3.reason: The condition short-circuits when expected is empty, so an empty FunctionalOptionsArgument would match any actual type without type checking.
